chunk_map.heading: Pick one threat, record the decision (H1/lede)
Phase 1: Run the threat scan across your mapped surface
Read the threat list, expect more than you'll use
Phase 2: Pick the one threat worth hardening against
Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation
Phase 3: Write the decision as an ADR
Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens
Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions
Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide leaning on a referent never named strands the reader mid-deck. Walked every candidate in reading order. Chunk 1 line 20 'The subagent does the walk' uses a definite noun two lines before line 22 first uses the word 'subagent' explicitly ('invoke the STRIDE skill as a subagent') -- but both sit in the SAME chunk, and the per-chunk test ("point at its antecedent INSIDE the chunk") does not impose within-chunk line ordering the way it does across chunks; a slide is read as one visual unit. Chunk 1 line 22 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' is explicit and self-naming (session-artifact carve-out; also verified as a real prior beat under rule 3). Chunk 6 lines 63-64 'The Decision section' / 'the Alternatives considered section' resolve against chunk 5's fenced prompt (line 79, 'Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives considered'), which precedes chunk 6 in reading order. Chunk 7 line 69 'the M3 worktree' / 'the side-quest' is unpacked in its own sentence ('The fork prompt called the worktree "the side-quest", and the scrollback has framed everything since as M3 work') so a reader needs no other file to follow it, on top of being genuinely earned in this same module's opening exercise. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found in any chunk.

Harm: pointing at another file by position only works if the deck starts where the writer assumed. Chunk 1 line 22 names the source by claim ('the access-surface map ... from Exercise 1') in one breath -- the claim itself carries the resolution, matching the rule's own worked PASS shape. Chunk 7 lines 68-69 name 'the fork prompt' and unpack its content in the same sentence ('called the worktree "the side-quest"') rather than locating it by position. No sentence points at a prior file solely by position ("the opening lecture said...") without also naming its claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a stranded callback sends the student hunting for a beat that was cut. Read earn-the-trust.md's current 'Start here' include list directly (not cached): '[Exercise: Open the side quest]' (line 33), '[Exercise: Map the access surface]' (line 37), this file (line 39), '[Exercise: Author your test-strategy skill]' (line 41). The push-back-moves table in that same module file labels these Ex1/Ex2/Ex3 respectively, confirming 'Exercise 1' at this file's line 22 means Map the access surface. Both backward references here ('the map you built' / 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' -> Map the access surface; 'the M3 worktree' / 'the side-quest' -> Open the side quest, which forks a worktree per that module's own What You'll Learn line 22) resolve to beats confirmed present in the live module file. The forward reference in the closer ('The next exercise authors a test-strategy skill') is not a rule-3 backward case, but also checks out against 'Author your test-strategy skill' at line 41.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess/predict beat whose answer is narrated above it teaches nothing. The only ask-then-reveal shape in the file is chunk 8: the ask (line 74, 'Ask Claude whether this ADR rides into future sessions automatically', plus the prompt fence at line 76) precedes the reveal (line 78, "Claude's answer: no...") in reading order, same chunk, correctly sequenced. No other guess/predict beat exists in the file.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. Checked the thinnest chunks specifically: chunk 2 (lines 29-30, 2 bullets) carries its own claim about why the scan over-produces and how to gauge scan depth; chunk 4 (lines 46-47, 2 bullets) carries the push-back rationale plus the land-the-mitigation instruction; chunk 6 (lines 63-64, 2 bullets) carries the voice-check plus the STRIDE-as-tool-not-lens worked example. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader. Checked all 9 '##' headers against their bodies: e.g. 'Check where the ADR landed' (line 66) -> body checks main-repo-vs-worktree path (lines 68-70); 'Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions' (line 72) -> body asks then answers exactly that (lines 74-79). Chunk 9's header ('Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear') covers the save instruction directly (lines 83-85); the trailing 'What happened:'/'What this sets up:' lines (87-89) are the standard architecture-mandated exercise-closer chrome, not a second competing claim the header would need to also cover. No contradiction found.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine-authored on a slide. Checked all sub-items across the full body: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple -- none ('One threat, not five' at line 36 is a single two-part contrast, not the banned three-part shape). (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples -- none. (c) self-grading superlatives -- none; grepped for 'most useful'/'one of the'-style phrasing, zero hits. (d) number+own-retraction -- none; the four time budgets (lines 3, 17, 34, 51) are plain durations with no hedge. (e) abstraction-noun stacks -- none; vocabulary stays concrete (access surface, incident story, ADR, worktree, diff). (f) verb triplets with an empty leg -- none. Aggregated into this one rule-7 entry per the completeness contract.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/authorial vocabulary a room can't parse. Grepped body for 'compendium', 'firing', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood', 'Connections' (proper noun) -- zero hits in body (all such terms appear only in the maintainer/backing blocks, which sit below the cut). 'Access surface'/'your mapped surface' (chunk 0 line 7, chunk 1 header) is domain-standard security vocabulary (cf. 'attack surface'), matching the rule's own carve-out distinguishing this from authorial 'surface'-as-writing-jargon. 'Main quest'/'side quest'/'worktree' are this module's own established teaching vocabulary, earned in the module's opening exercise, not leaked internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: over-bolding trains readers to ignore bold as a signal. Every bold span in the body is short (<=3 words) label chrome: chunk 0's **Time:**/**Window:**/**What you do:**/**What you build:**/**The point:**, chunk 9's **Worth keeping?**/**What happened:**/**What this sets up:**. The 2026-07-09 emphasis-pass maintainer note (raw line 97) names five of these seven explicitly as untouched chrome; 'Worth keeping?' and the pair 'What happened:'/'What this sets up:' function identically (question/label lead-ins on their own line, not narrative sentences) and were left alone by that same pass, consistent with treating them the same way. Scanned every bullet lead across all 9 chunks for a bolded whole-sentence lead (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture shape) -- none found; no chunk carries more than one narrative-bold element (the chrome labels are structural, not narrative).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the deck gets rules 1-9 applied to a slide that never renders. This file is included in earn-the-trust.md (verified live, line 39: '[Exercise: Threat-model with STRIDE](exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md)'), the same include shape every AE101 exercise uses to reach the composed deck via .phase--exercise wrapping. No phase-less bare prose section exists in this file -- the whole body sits under the exercise wrapper by construction. The mechanical checks for rules 11/12/14 (below) ran directly against this file path and all reported per-file results, corroborating it is a recognized slide-bearing unit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading inside an exercise where none is earned muddies the imperative/phase-label mood exercises need. Checked all 9 '##' headings verbatim: 3 are 'Phase N: <label>' phase labels, 6 are imperative verb phrases ('Read the threat list, expect more than you'll use'; 'Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation'; 'Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens'; 'Check where the ADR landed'; 'Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions'; 'Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear'). None is a bare declarative claim; this exercise has no law/consolidation moment that would earn one. Consistent exercise mood throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a doctrine restatement / self-referential design note / aphorism kicker adds no move, object, tell, or priority the slide doesn't already carry. This file's own 2026-08-25 lean-pass maintainer note (raw line 93) already cut six near-miss instances of exactly this shape ('It will have more entries than you want to deal with.', 'You are picking a single threat worth hardening against.', 'You save it as the ADR next.', the Phase-3 compliance-checkbox duplicate, half the worktree-inference bullet, 'Not everything survived to disk.', the closer's CISO line). Closest surviving candidate, examined and kept: chunk 3 lines 37-38 'The agent proposes the incident story; you judge whether it fits. You are not inventing the worst case from scratch. Claude drafts it; your read of your own codebase decides whether it's real.' -- the third sentence echoes the first in different words, but it adds a fact the first sentence doesn't carry (the judgment is grounded specifically in codebase familiarity, not judgment-in-the-abstract), which is the mechanism behind the middle sentence's reassurance ('not inventing from scratch'). It stays inside the rule, narrowly -- flagged separately as a TODO for the maintainer's eye, not filed as a rule violation. Also checked chunk 2 line 29 ('that rejection is the point, not a failure of the scan') against the lede's 'STRIDE's value is rejection, not enumeration' (chunk 0 line 11): the chunk-2 line applies the doctrine at the exact moment the student feels the long list and adds a new instruction ('you reject most of its entries in the next phase') the lede doesn't carry -- kept. No surviving instance of self-referential design commentary or aphorism kicker found.
